chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umeyr, all together, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the zakat: 'Is it preferable to give to some of those who do not ask, over others?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the one who does not ask is preferable to the one who asks.'
ai.seo_question: Who is more deserving of zakat: those who ask for it or those who do not?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the preference for the non-asker (ghair al-sa'il) over the active beggar (sa'il) is rooted in the preservation of personal dignity (karamah) and the prevention of dependency. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on encouraging self-reliance among the poor while ensuring the efficient distribution of zakat funds to those who are truly in need but maintain their modesty.
